t: A1C
s: A blood test showing average blood sugar over about 3 months.

t: Basal insulin
s: Long-acting insulin that covers background needs between meals and overnight.

t: BMI
s: Body mass index — weight in kilograms divided by height in metres squared.

t: Boxed warning
s: The FDA's strongest label warning.

t: Compounded drug
s: A drug mixed by a pharmacy for a patient; not FDA-approved.

t: GIP
s: Glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide — a gut hormone targeted by tirzepatide.

t: GLP-1
s: Glucagon-like peptide-1 — a gut hormone that raises insulin, lowers appetite and slows digestion.

t: Half-life
s: Time for the amount of a drug in the body to fall by half.

t: Hypoglycemia
s: Low blood sugar.

t: MASH
s: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis — a form of fatty liver disease.

t: MTC
s: Medullary thyroid carcinoma — the cancer named in GLP-1 boxed warnings.

t: Off-label
s: Use of a drug for a purpose not on its approved label.

t: Prior authorization
s: Insurer approval needed before a drug is covered.

t: Titration
s: Gradual dose increases to improve tolerance.
